headline: Treasure Coast traffic report: I-95 ramp closures, overnight road work planned Aug. 21-28
teaser: Drivers across the Treasure Coast should prepare for overnight I-95 ramp closures, major lane restrictions and local road closures through Aug. 28, including work at Kanner Highway, High Meadow Avenue, Gatlin Boulevard and several Port St. Lucie roads.
body:
Drivers across Martin, St. Lucie and Indian River counties should prepare for another week of construction-related lane and ramp closures as Florida Department of Transportation projects continue throughout the Treasure Coast.

Several of the most significant impacts are scheduled along Interstate 95, including overnight closures at Kanner Highway and High Meadow Avenue in Martin County and at Tradition Parkway/Gatlin Boulevard in Port St. Lucie.

Here are the major traffic impacts scheduled for Aug. 21 through Aug. 28.

MARTIN COUNTY

I-95 at Kanner Highway and High Meadow Avenue

Drivers traveling through Martin County will encounter extensive overnight work on I-95 beginning Sunday, Aug. 23.

Southbound I-95 between Bridge Road and the Martin-St. Lucie county line is scheduled to have two lanes closed from 7:30 p.m. to 5:30 a.m. Sunday through Friday. Northbound I-95 along the same stretch will have two lanes closed from 8:30 p.m. to 6:30 a.m. Crews are performing milling, resurfacing and signage work.

The southbound I-95 exit ramp to Kanner Highway, Exit 101, is scheduled to close from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday, Aug. 23, through Friday, Aug. 28. Drivers will be directed south to Bridge Road, then back north on I-95 to reach Kanner Highway.

The southbound entrance ramp from Kanner Highway to I-95 is also scheduled for overnight closures during the same period. Drivers will be detoured using Pratt Whitney Road and Bridge Road.

Additional overnight closures are planned at High Meadow Avenue. The southbound I-95 exit and entrance ramps at High Meadow Avenue are scheduled to close at various times from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday through Friday.

The northbound I-95 exit ramp to High Meadow Avenue is scheduled to close from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Thursday, Aug. 27, for overhead sign installation.

FDOT says only one of the affected ramps will be closed at a time.

U.S. 1 in Stuart

Northbound and southbound U.S. 1 between SE Fischer Street and SE Decker Avenue will have two lanes closed intermittently from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday, Aug. 23, through Friday, Aug. 28, for sign installation.

A1A near Jensen Beach

One lane of A1A/NE Ocean Boulevard between NE Shore Village Terrace and the Jensen Beach Causeway may close intermittently Monday through Friday for pavement widening and drainage work. Two-way traffic will be maintained by flaggers.

SW Martin Highway

SW Martin Highway between SW Stuart West Boulevard and Citrus Boulevard will have intermittent single-lane closures from 7 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday through Thursday for milling and resurfacing. Flaggers will maintain two-way traffic.

Additional utility-related lane closures are also planned in Palm City, Stuart, Port Mayaca and Indiantown during the week.

ST. LUCIE COUNTY

I-95 near Gatlin Boulevard and Tradition Parkway

Northbound and southbound I-95 between Gatlin Boulevard and just south of Becker Road will have two lanes closed, with possible lane shifts, from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday, Aug. 23, through Friday, Aug. 28, as crews continue milling and repaving operations.

The southbound I-95 entrance ramp from Tradition Parkway/Gatlin Boulevard is scheduled to close from 7:30 p.m. to 5:30 a.m. Wednesday, Aug. 26, and Thursday, Aug. 27. Drivers will be detoured south on Village Parkway to Becker Road, where they can enter southbound I-95.

FDOT is also giving advance notice of southbound I-95 ramp closures at Becker Road beginning Aug. 31 and continuing into early September.

Port St. Lucie Boulevard neighborhood closures

Construction on the SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard widening project will create several significant local impacts.

One lane of SW Port St. Lucie Boulevard between SW Jordin Avenue and SW Alcantarra Boulevard may close intermittently from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. Monday through Friday.

A series of side roads along the corridor may also close for drainage and utility work. The affected roads include SW Jaslo Avenue, SW Jacoby Avenue, SW McCullough Avenue, SW McCall Road, SW McHord Avenue, SW Paar Drive, SW Koler Avenue and SW McDevitt Avenue.

Some of those closures may begin at 7 a.m. Monday and remain in effect until 5 p.m. Friday. FDOT says adjacent roads will not be closed at the same time, and access to homes and businesses will be maintained.

Port St. Lucie Boulevard and U.S. 1

Drivers should also expect daytime and overnight lane closures on SE Port St. Lucie Boulevard between SE Seafury Lane and SE Lennard Road and on U.S. 1 between SE Jennings Road and NW Golden Oak Trail.

Crews are working on drainage, sidewalks, erosion control, milling and repaving as part of the ongoing resurfacing project.

Midway Road

One lane of Midway Road between Florida's Turnpike and Selvitz Road may close intermittently from 9 a.m. to 4 p.m. through September as the widening project continues.

Fort Pierce and North Causeway area

Several long-term construction impacts remain around the new A1A North Causeway Bridge. The new bridge opened to traffic in May, while work continues around U.S. 1, Old Dixie Highway and Juanita Avenue.

Drivers should expect intermittent lane closures in the area through September. The old drawbridge has been permanently closed to vehicles and is being demolished as part of the remaining construction.

Additional utility and maintenance work is scheduled on U.S. 1, Okeechobee Road, Ocean Drive and other Fort Pierce corridors during the week.

INDIAN RIVER COUNTY

Oslo Road and I-95

Construction continues on the new I-95 interchange at Oslo Road and the widening of Oslo Road.

One lane in each direction of Oslo Road from about 1,500 feet west of I-95 to SW 58th Avenue will remain closed around the clock through September. One travel lane will remain open in each direction.

Nighttime lane closures are also scheduled beginning Aug. 24 on 66th Avenue, 74th Avenue, 82nd Avenue and 58th Avenue near Oslo Road.

I-95 within the project limits may have as many as two lanes closed nightly from 9 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday through Thursday.

Sebastian River High School area

The southbound roadway at the Sebastian River High School entrances to Shark Boulevard and Mako Way is scheduled to close from 8 a.m. to 4 p.m. Saturday, Aug. 22, and Sunday, Aug. 23, for repaving.

Elsewhere along the SR 510 widening project, one lane may close intermittently between Sebastian Boulevard and 87th Street from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday through Friday.

Sebastian Inlet

Drivers using A1A/Jimmy Buffett Memorial Highway around Sebastian Inlet State Park may encounter single-lane or shoulder closures as construction continues on the $101.9 million Sebastian Inlet Bridge replacement project.

Only one lane will be closed at a time, with flaggers directing traffic. Partial closures of the north and south parking lots at Sebastian Inlet State Park also remain in effect for the long-term bridge project.

Vero Beach

A1A between Mango Road and Shoe Drive will have intermittent overnight lane closures from 8 p.m. to 6 a.m. Sunday through Thursday for milling and paving.

Additional utility-related lane closures are planned on A1A and U.S. 1 in the Vero Beach and Sebastian areas.

Drivers should allow extra travel time in work zones and watch for changing traffic patterns and posted detours. Construction schedules may change because of weather or other unforeseen conditions. Real-time interstate traffic information is available through FL511.

headline: Port St. Lucie schedules Sept. 2-3 stakeholder meetings on 2050 Mobility Plan, fee updates
teaser: Port St. Lucie will host two stakeholder meetings Sept. 2 and 3 to discuss proposed updates to its 2050 Mobility Plan and Mobility Fee Schedule, with in-person and virtual attendance options.
body:
The City of Port St. Lucie will hold two stakeholder meetings in September to discuss proposed updates to its 2050 Mobility Plan and Mobility Fee Schedule, which are intended to help guide future transportation and mobility improvements across the city.

City officials said the sessions will give stakeholders an opportunity to hear updates on the proposals and provide input.

## Meeting schedule

The first meeting is scheduled for Wednesday, Sept. 2, from 6 to 7:45 p.m. at the Port St. Lucie Community Center, 2195 SE Airoso Blvd.

A second meeting will be held Thursday, Sept. 3, from 10 a.m. to noon in the City Hall Council Chambers, 121 SW Port St. Lucie Blvd.

Both sessions also can be attended virtually. Residents and other stakeholders who want to participate online can [RSVP for a virtual meeting](https://dxajyacab.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=0016H91ytg38ubjigDWGOO3PaWpQRW69EwrOeXC84vdoDqqbFDQbjeKWnxsn8-ohcMlpSG473Al2zC9afQvoMMfm-RuBR8kVkh2PAXnBauu94Ve4VpV957cmCoMtfMeb1kXoZF1tS3Ep0O-ytAFmki7Jlupayh2_pf_eTT4XZwSQ_Y=&c=9F8DBte94EMdgM-12z0zWEOwJ6a_L9BVBhJCKOXS0j0x5yxH-R8QPw==&ch=2CrZlTWehszSBl0t32xkBooOKl4rDMNPJbgpw6cevIhhtFBtACtQUg==).

## What the city is reviewing

The proposed 2050 Mobility Plan and Mobility Fee Schedule updates are part of the city's planning for future transportation and mobility needs. The stakeholder meetings are designed to provide an update on that work and collect public input before the process moves forward.

headline: Port St. Lucie seeks artists for Botanical Gardens sculptures, photographers for utility box wraps
teaser: Port St. Lucie is seeking Florida artists for two temporary Botanical Gardens sculptures and local photographers for a utility box wrap project celebrating the city's natural environment.
body:
The City of Port St. Lucie is inviting artists and photographers to take part in two public art initiatives focused on nature and the city's visual landscape. One opportunity seeks temporary sculptures for the Port St. Lucie Botanical Gardens, while the other will use original photography to refresh utility box wraps at traffic intersections.

## Botanical Gardens sculpture installations

The Friends of the Port St. Lucie Botanical Gardens are seeking two existing garden- or nature-themed sculptures for temporary display for 18 months. Installation is planned by Nov. 20, 2026.

One sculpture will be placed at the Botanical Gardens entrance and the second will be displayed in the rose garden. The opportunity is open only to Florida-based artists.

The City's announcement lists Aug. 12 as the deadline for questions and Sept. 11 as the deadline for RFQ submissions. Artists can review the [full Botanical Gardens RFP](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1C8NvS9sx811LVO31GzD73ngOgpPvhiI3/view). Questions may be sent to [publicart@designinglocal.com](mailto:publicart@designinglocal.com).

## Utility box wrap photography project

The City is also inviting professional and amateur photographers of all ages to submit original photographs for utility box wraps at traffic intersections. The project is intended to place art in unexpected public spaces while replacing existing wraps with new nature-centered designs.

Photographers must have a connection to Port St. Lucie by living, working, attending school or worshiping in the city. Each participant may submit one original photograph in high-resolution, landscape-orientation JPG format. The City is looking for images that reflect local wildlife, native vegetation and Port St. Lucie's landscapes and biodiversity.

Submissions are being accepted through Oct. 2, 2026. Entries should include the photographer's name, contact information and artwork title; minors also must include guardian contact information. Submissions should be emailed to [bgrubbs@cityofpsl.com](mailto:bgrubbs@cityofpsl.com).

The City's Public Art Advisory Board will evaluate submissions for photographic quality, thematic relevance, printability and suitability for utility box wraps. Final selections will be recommended to the City Council. Approved artists will be recognized on the City's website, and selected work could be used by the City for up to seven years. Each completed wrap will include a designated 16-inch-by-16-inch area for the artist's signature.

More information about both opportunities is available on the [City of Port St. Lucie's call for artists page](https://www.cityofpsl.com/News-Stories/2026/Call-for-Artists-Botanical-Gardens-Sculptures-and-Utility-Box-Wraps). Artists and photographers also can contact the City's Planning & Zoning Department at 772-871-5212 or [bgrubbs@cityofpsl.com](mailto:bgrubbs@cityofpsl.com).
